chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi and Abu Talib, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
O Allah, You are my reliance in every worry,
and You are my hope in every difficulty, and You are for me in every matter that befalls me, a Trustworthy and a Resource.

How many worries are there such that the heart weakens from them, and plans become scarce regarding them, and the near and far ones abandon them, and the enemies gloat with them, and the affairs exhaust me in them.
I revealed it to You and complained of it to You, turning away from those besides You. Therefore, relieve it, remove it, and suffice for me regarding it.
For You are the Patron of every bounty and the Companion of every need, and the End-point of every desire. So, for You is abundant praise, and for You is the overflowing favor.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for reliance on God in times of difficulty?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication (du'a) from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) serves as a comprehensive model for seeking divine aid during calamities, emphasizing total reliance (tawakkul) on Allah when human efforts and social support fail. It highlights the theological concept of shifting from self-reliance to absolute dependence on God, acknowledging Him as the ultimate source of relief and sufficiency. This text is frequently cited in Shia devotional practices to cultivate spiritual resilience and gratitude during times of hardship.
